key_insight: EHR foundation models showed weak cohort-level memorisation but no reliable patient-level disclosure under the evaluated attacks.
clinical_relevance: Privacy audits must distinguish patient-specific memorisation from predictable clinical patterns when assessing EHR model disclosure risks.
method: Evaluated GPT-2-style models trained on MIMIC-IV at early, best-validation, and final checkpoints.
Tested fixed-window token reconstruction, sensitive-attribute disclosure, and random patient-level canary recovery.
Used an overfit 1,000-patient model as a positive control for strong memorisation.
evidence_signal: Training-patient canary recovery AUROC rose from 0.512 to 0.549 while held-out recovery stayed at chance; the overfit positive control achieved near-perfect recovery.
watch_item: These findings do not establish privacy safety beyond the evaluated models, prompts, and attacks.
paper_title: Constructing and Validating Memorisation Audits for EHR Foundation Models
